description: The DELTA Light Coastal Run is an atmospheric light spectacle along the coastline from Domburg to Zoutelande. Decked out with lights, colour and sound, participants cover the final 11 kilometres of the course, with runners and walkers bringing Friday evening to a festive close together. DJs and light and sound effects create a unique atmosphere along the way. The finish is in Zoutelande, where a welcoming atmosphere awaits.
course_highlights: 11 kilometres along the coastline from Domburg to Zoutelande
Light, colour and sound effects along the way
A festive finish with DJs and a unique atmosphere
additional: Race number sent in mid-September; race number printed with first name; wear race number on chest; bus ticket from Zoutelande to Domburg for the start, € 5,- (recommended); time limit 3 hours (until 22:45); start location: car park at Duinstraat / Van Voorthuijzenstraat in Domburg; race numbers for participants from abroad can be collected in advance at the festival tent on Langstraat in Zoutelande on 1 October, 18:00–20:00, and 2 October, 16:00–18:30; tip: bring your own light, as none are sold on site; parking in Zoutelande at the football field, Wulkpad or Kustlicht (paid parking until 19:00); parking in Domburg at various car parks with sufficient capacity. 11 km course, starts on Friday evening, no changing or shower facilities, maximum 2000 participants, registration opens on 1 January, race numbers sent in September.

name: Pieken+Dalen Festival
location: RCN het Grote Bos, Doorn, Utrecht, Netherlands
description: On Saturday, October 3, 2026, the very first Pieken+Dalen Festival will take place at RCN het Grote Bos in Doorn, organized by Stichting DiabetesPlus. This unique event combines walking and running over a range of distances, from a 5-kilometer loop to a marathon, in the beautiful Utrechtse Heuvelrug. After the effort, a warm welcome awaits at the festival grounds, with opportunities to meet, music, a Buddy Tent, a Q&A with diabetes researchers, a TechTent, and various food trucks. The festival offers a special opportunity to face the peaks and valleys of blood sugar together with friends, family, and fellow athletes in a welcoming and inclusive setting.
course_highlights: A range of walking and running distances from 5 km to a marathon
The beautiful, hilly natural landscape of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug
Festival grounds with music, a playground, and diabetes technology
additional: After the sporting activities, the festival grounds feature a Buddy Tent, a Q&A with diabetes researchers, a TechTent showcasing the latest diabetes technology, musical performances by people with type 1 diabetes, a playground for children, a prize raffle, and various food trucks serving food and drinks. Walking and running activities, technology and social activities, food trucks, family- and child-friendly

name: 11e Molenloop (Molensmooiste) Alblasserdam-Kinderdijk
description: Molensmooiste is a unique running race taking place on Saturday, 3 October 2026, at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Kinderdijk. Participants run past all the area’s iconic windmills. The 10 English Miles consists of two laps, while the 5 English Miles is one lap. The start and finish are in the heart of the windmill area, making for a special and atmospheric experience. With a limit of 1,500 participants and organised under the auspices of AAA Atletiekvereniging Alblasserdam, it is an event for both recreational and competitive runners.
course_highlights: The route really does pass all the windmills of Kinderdijk
The 10 English Miles consists of two 8 km laps through the windmill area
Start and finish in the heart of the UNESCO World Heritage Site
additional: The start and finish are in the heart of the windmill area, with pace-based waves because the start path is narrow. Race numbers and shoe tags can be collected from 07:00 in the runners’ village, no later than 09:00. There is one drinks station per lap. The Kids Run takes place on Wednesday, 30 September 2026, at the AAA Atletiekbaan Alblasserdam and is free; registration is available on site. The race includes wave starts for different distances, is part of the Grote Rivieren Loopcircuit, and registration is open until maximum capacity is reached. Late registration is not possible.

name: Kûbaarder Hurdrindei
description: The Kûbaarder Hurdrindei is a well-known running and recreational running event in Friesland, held annually on the first Saturday of October. The course follows quiet, low-traffic paths and roads, including the historic Slachtedijk and the “griene dyk” dating from 1200. There are three distances: 5 km, 11.2 km and a half marathon of 21.1 km, plus a free Kidzzrun for children over 1 and 2 km. After the run, participants can relax with a cup of hot broth and enjoy a friendly chat. The event attracts 120 to 140 participants each year and is open to runners of all levels, including people with disabilities.
course_highlights: Course along the historic Slachtedijk (the old Middelzee dike, dating from around 1100 AD)
Quiet, low-traffic paths and roads
Routes along the winding “griene dyk” dating from 1200
additional: Maximum of 250 participants. Race numbers can be collected on 3 October from 11:30 to 12:30 at Petronella Moenstrjitte 22. Late registration is available at the village hall between 12:00 and 13:00; late registration closes at 13:00. The Kidsrun starts at 13:00; all other distances start at 13:10. Race numbers are colour-coded by distance. Medals can be collected after the event. Event date: 3 October 2026; approximately 100 participants in 2025; weather conditions can be challenging.

name: Midden Drenthe Loop
location: Camping Midden Drenthe, Zwiggelte, Midden-Drenthe, Drenthe, Netherlands
description: The Midden Drenthe Loop is an annual running race organised by Loopgroep Westerbork, with its 36th edition scheduled for Saturday, 3 October 2026. The event offers two distances, 5 and 10 kilometres, and starts and finishes at Camping Midden Drenthe in Zwiggelte. The routes pass through the beautiful countryside of Midden Drenthe. The 5 km route is entirely paved, while the 10 km route includes a short stretch of sandy path. The race is open to participants aged 12 and over, and finishers receive a medal.
course_highlights: The 5 km route is entirely paved
The 10 km route includes a short stretch of sandy path
Start and finish at Camping Midden Drenthe in Zwiggelte
additional: The minimum age to participate is 12. Participants receive a medal at the finish. Cancellations are free of charge up to 14 days before the race. Results are based on net time, measured using a timing system. Pets and baby carriers are not allowed. The route passes through Midden Drenthe and includes paved sections and a sandy path. Registration is via an online form.

name: Molens Mooiste
description: Molensmooiste is a unique running race taking place on Saturday 3 October 2026 at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Kinderdijk. Participants run through the iconic windmill area, with the start and finish in the heart of this beautiful landscape. The race offers two distances, 5 English Miles (8 km) and 10 English Miles (16 km), with this year’s routes passing all the windmills of Kinderdijk. Starts take place in waves because of the narrow start path, so everyone can make the most of the windmill experience. The event is organised under the auspices of athletics club AAA Alblasserdam and attracts around 1,500 participants.
course_highlights: Route passes all the windmills of Kinderdijk
Start and finish in the heart of the UNESCO World Heritage Site
100% asphalt course with one drinks station per lap
additional: Race number and shoe tag will be ready at the runners’ village; collect them by 09:00 at the latest. Starts take place in waves because of the narrow start path. The runners’ village opens at 07:00. After finishing, participants receive a medal and a windmill map. Optional extras: an event shirt (€24,95) and a running cap (€14,95); order by 19 September 2026 at the latest. Registration is open while places remain, up to a maximum of 1,500 participants. The event starts at 09:30 and offers a unique experience through a landscape of windmills and UNESCO World Heritage.

name: Rondje Lindewijk
description: Rondje Lindewijk is a friendly running event in rural Lindewijk, Drenthe, taking place on October 3, 2026. The race offers various distances from 0.5 km to 16.1 km, including special kids’ runs and racerunner categories, making it accessible to runners of all ages and levels. The course is flat and runs through the village, ideal for building a steady pace. The organizer, Start78, creates a warm village atmosphere and offers the option to order a unique Rondje Lindewijk shirt when registering.
course_highlights: Flat course through the village of Lindewijk
Distances ranging from 0.5 km to 16.1 km
Special racerunner categories
additional: Order your Rondje Lindewijk shirt in good time when registering to make sure you receive it. Flat course through the village; registration via the official page; includes kids’ runs and racerunner categories.

description: Rondje om de Koepel is a popular running event in Lunteren and the surrounding area. The route takes participants past the Centre of the Netherlands, over the Goudsberg and through the Lunteren Community Forest, with its distinctive Koepel. The event offers three distances: a 1 km Kids’ Run, a 5 km run and a challenging 10 km run. The course is mostly on forest trails, with climbs and descents. The event is professionally supported, with warm-up sessions and care provided by Therapeutisch Centrum Lunteren. It also supports local charities, making it both a sporting and community-minded event.
course_highlights: Run past the Centre of the Netherlands
Forest-trail course with climbs and descents
Run through the Lunteren Community Forest and over the Goudsberg
additional: A warm-up led by Therapeutisch Centrum Lunteren begins 10 minutes before each start. Changing facilities are available at recreation centre De Goudsberg. Parking is available nearby, with traffic marshals; participants from Lunteren are encouraged to cycle. First-aid providers and traffic marshals are stationed along the course to ensure safety. €3.50 of each participant’s entry fee is donated to a local charity; this year, it is Woonzorgcentrum De Honskamp. Run past the Centre of the Netherlands on a route through woodland with climbs and descents. Advance registration is available. The start location is recreation centre De Goudsberg, where parking and changing facilities are available.

name: Valley Run
location: Winkelcentrum de Ellekoot, Veenendaal, Utrecht, Netherlands
distance_verbose: Halve marathon, 15 km, 10 km, 5 km, 1.2 km
description: The Schuiteman Valley Run is a running event in Veenendaal, starting at the Ellekoot shopping centre. The 10th edition has been moved to Saturday, 3 October 2026, due to extremely high temperatures. Five distances are offered, including the 1.2-kilometre Etos Bijl Kids Run and a new half marathon, the Davelaar Sport Half Marathon. The event offers a great opportunity to experience the Utrechtse Heuvelrug and is suitable for a range of ages and fitness levels.
course_highlights: Start at the Ellekoot shopping centre
Five distances, including a kids’ run and a half marathon
Experience the Utrechtse Heuvelrug
additional: Five distances are available, including a 1.2 km kids’ run and a new half marathon. The start is at the Ellekoot shopping centre. The date has been moved to 3 October 2026 due to extremely high temperatures. The event promotes community spirit and fitness, with both the start and finish in Veenendaal.

name: Hoge Veluwe Wandeldag
location: Nationale Park De Hoge Veluwe, Otterlo, Gelderland, Netherlands
distance_verbose: Halve marathon, 15 km, 10 km, 5 km, 1 km
organizer: Het Nationale Park De Hoge Veluwe
description: The Hoge Veluwe Walking Day takes place in the beautiful Hoge Veluwe National Park, a green treasure trove of the Netherlands with varied landscapes, unique flora and fauna, and distinctive art and culture. On this day, walkers can enjoy the park’s many walking routes, including special anniversary routes and the historic Boundary Marker Route. The park offers a unique combination of nature and culture, with iconic places such as the Kröller-Müller Museum and St. Hubertus Hunting Lodge. The Hoge Veluwe Walking Day is an ideal opportunity to discover nature and enjoy a day of peace and inspiration.

The route passes through dunes and along the beach, offering a unique combination of nature and sport. The Coastal Marathon itself is known as the most beautiful and toughest marathon in the Netherlands, with challenging climbs, wind and stunning sea views. The Ladies Run offers an accessible running experience for women, with 5- and 10-kilometre distances starting and finishing in Zoutelande. The event is a sporting highlight in Zeeland, with a festive atmosphere and a heroes’ welcome at the finish.
course_highlights: Route through dunes and along the beach, with sea views
Starts in Burgh-Haamstede and finishes in Zoutelande
Challenging climbs and wind as natural elements
additional: Race numbers are sent by post in mid-September. Race numbers for participants with an overseas address can be collected in advance in Zoutelande. The Walking Marathon starts between 7:00 and 8:30, with no wave starts. Buses from Zoutelande to Burgh-Haamstede depart promptly at 6:30. The finish closes at 18:00. The Ladies Run starts at 17:40, and timing ends at 19:45. Parking is organised and signposted; paid parking applies in some car parks. The course is 42 km, starting in Burgh-Haamstede and finishing in Zoutelande. Registration opens on 1 January. Information is available about transport and parking, refreshments along the route, and the 18:00 time limit.

The half-marathon route passes several highlights, including Tankenberg, Wilmersberg, Hakenberg and Paasberg. It is mostly paved, with drink stations every 5 kilometers. The race is suitable for both individual runners and corporate teams, and has a time limit of 2 hours and 30 minutes. Alongside the half marathon, there are also 10-kilometer and 5-kilometer races, a corporate race and school races, making the event accessible to a wide audience.

Mostly paved course with drink stations every 5 kilometers

The event is popular with local and recreational runners.

The race offers several distances, including 3.3 km, 7 km, 14 km, and a half marathon of 21.1 km, making it suitable for recreational and more experienced runners alike. The event takes place on Sunday, October 4, 2026, and is organized by AV Dem. The atmosphere is sporty and challenging, with a playful theme that lets participants compete to become the “ruler of Heemskerk.”

With various distances, including an 8 km race, a KidsRun and a Business Run, the event offers a suitable challenge for every runner. The scenic course and sporting community make this a festive and professionally organised running experience in Drachten. The 22nd edition takes place on Sunday, 4 October 2026.

Distances for all ages, including the KidsRun and Business Run
Sporting community and professional organisation

Prize-giving takes place shortly after each distance next to the finish

This annual family running event, organised by Sportclub Antilope, offers something for everyone: a 1.3 km Kids Run for children up to 12 years old and 5 km and 10 km races for runners aged 12 and over. The route is a 5-kilometre loop, run twice for the 10 km. The event is known for its friendly atmosphere and sporting achievements, and welcomes both beginners and experienced runners.

name: ASML Marathon Eindhoven
description: The ASML Marathon Eindhoven is the largest two-day sporting event in North Brabant and takes place annually on the second weekend of October. The event offers a wide range of running distances, including the marathon, half marathon, quarter marathon and various other runs for all ages. The course is flat, wide and atmospheric, with a finish in the center of Eindhoven, making for fast times and a unique experience. The city is entirely focused on sport, innovation and connection, with enthusiastic supporters lining the course. This makes the ASML Marathon Eindhoven a festive and internationally acclaimed running event.
course_highlights: Flat, wide course with a finish in the center of Eindhoven
Atmospheric course with enthusiastic crowd support
Route past iconic spots in the city
additional: Participants receive a unique medal. A limited-edition running shirt is available. Special “Run Against Cancer” initiatives allow participants to raise funds and receive a unique shirt. Race bibs for participants from the Netherlands are available until September 1. The finish is on the lively Vestdijk in the center of Eindhoven. This two-day event offers registration for various distances, with the start and finish in the center of Eindhoven, and includes an urban walk and children’s activities.

The event takes place around the Sloterplas and offers a scenic running experience in an urban setting.

5 km and 10 km distances available
Kids’ runs for young runners

description: The Janlouterloop is an annual running event in Vlaardingen’s Broekpolder, organised in memory of Jan Louter, a passionate runner and coach who died of pancreatic cancer in 2024. Participants can choose from three running distances (5, 10 and 15 kilometres) or a 10-kilometre walk. The event is organised by AV Fortuna and supports the charity ‘Support Casper’, part of the Stichting Overleven met Alvleesklierkanker. The Janlouterloop combines sport, camaraderie and an experience of nature in a unique polder setting.

additional: Proceeds from the event go to the charity ‘Support Casper’, part of the Stichting Overleven met Alvleesklierkanker. The race features a fast and spectacular 1-kilometre route through the city centre, with an accessible programme for all ages, including kids’ runs, a family run and a business run. The day concludes with a final in which the fastest recreational runners compete against national and international elite athletes. The event combines sporting spirit with a festive atmosphere and is open to everyone, including athletes with a disability.

An event for all ages, with registration via the website, including an activity area and prizes.

name: LoveLife Run Amsterdam
description: LoveLife Run Amsterdam is a special running event taking place on October 10 at the Olympic Stadium. Courageous current and former cancer patients run 5 or 10 kilometers alongside their loved ones and healthcare providers to raise money for groundbreaking cancer research. Everyone is welcome to take part or support the participants, including people who have not had cancer themselves. The event combines an athletic challenge with a powerful message of hope and involvement.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the iconic Olympic Stadium Amsterdam
Distances of 5 km and 10 km for participants and their loved ones
Group warm-up and a finish-line cheque presentation
additional: Participants receive a LoveLife Run sports shirt and a medal. A 12-week training program is available under the guidance of specialist trainers. After the run, there is a group cheque presentation. The event recommends using public transport or cycling because of congestion and parking costs around the Olympic Stadium. The event is open to everyone, including current and former cancer patients, their family, friends, and healthcare providers. It focuses on recovery, self-confidence, and a sense of community, with a special emphasis on support and fundraising for cancer research.

The routes pass through the village and the beautiful surrounding countryside, by the medieval castle, the grain mill, Hernense Forest and rural Leur. The event is suitable for all ages and offers a sporty, convivial afternoon with a warm atmosphere and plenty of spectators along the route.

Prize ceremonies take place at 14:30 for the youth distances and at 16:15 for the 5 km and 10 km. The best Hernen resident receives a special prize. 5 and 10 kilometre routes through the countryside around Vollenhove
Beautiful natural surroundings with well-marked paths
additional: Race numbers can be collected on Friday evening, 9 October, from 19:30 to 20:30, or on race day from 09:00 to 10:30 at the start location. Ample parking and changing and shower facilities are available. First aid is available along the route and at the start/finish during the race. Timekeeping is done with the IPICO chip system; chips are distributed with race numbers and must be returned after the race. Prizes are awarded based on gun times. Registration until 8 October 2026, use of the IPICO chip system, free shirt for early registration, parking and first aid available

name: Run2Day Vlinderloop
location: Korfbal Vereniging Victum, Houten, Utrecht, Netherlands
description: The Run2Day Vlinderloop in Houten is a monthly performance run held on the second Saturday of every month from September through May. The route runs through the countryside around Houten, passing sights including Heemstede Castle and the Amsterdam–Rhine Canal, and offers a lovely mix of nature and culture. There are several distances, from 5.2 km to the half marathon, and the event is suitable for both children and adults. The start is at Korfbal Vereniging Victum, and the atmosphere is friendly and sporty, with an emphasis on running together and having fun.
course_highlights: A beautiful course through the countryside around Houten, passing Heemstede Castle and the Amsterdam–Rhine Canal
Route along the Kromme Rijn and through Amelisweerd
Almost entirely paved course with clear route signs and arrows
additional: There is a 2,500-metre SAMSAMLOOP, where you run with another person and cross the finish line together. There is also a team run in which four runners finish together. Race numbers can be collected from 16:00 on the day of the run. Digital late registration is available until 18:00 on the day of the run, as long as the maximum number of participants has not been reached. There are water stations along the course and a warm-up for the different distances. The route is not entirely closed to traffic, but it is clearly marked with route signs and arrows. A monthly performance run with different distances, suitable for recreational and competitive runners.

name: 1 E.Mijl in line 7e editie
description: The 1 E.Mijl in line 7th edition is a running event in Klaaswaal with a distance of 1.6 kilometers. The event offers a unique opportunity to improve your personal best in a friendly and sporty atmosphere. The race is suitable for runners looking to cover a short, fast distance. Registration is available via an external website, and the event is part of ProRun’s running calendar.
course_highlights: Distance of 1.6 km
Held in Klaaswaal
7th edition of the event
additional: Limited number of participants (100), start on Rijksstraatweg, potentially rainy weather in October, categories for men, women and youth

name: AVW 3bossentrail
description: The AVW 3Bossentrail takes place on 10 October 2026 in Wieringerwerf and passes through three forests in the Wieringermeer. The routes range from 14 to 28 kilometres and follow walking paths, singletracks and boardwalks, with the course on unpaved surfaces wherever possible. There is also a 14 km canitrail, where dogs must be kept on a lead. The trail run focuses on enjoying nature rather than competition, and staggered start groups are used to ensure a calm start in the forest.
course_highlights: Trail through three forests in the Wieringermeer
Routes follow walking paths, singletracks and boardwalks
Course is unpaved wherever possible
additional: Staggered start groups are used so participants can enter the forest at a relaxed pace. There is no timekeeping during the trail run; competition is not the focus. The organisers ask participants to bring their own cup to help preserve nature. The canitrail can be shortened to approximately 12 km, and dogs must be kept on a lead. Trail through three forests, unpaved paths, canitrail, no timekeeping, staggered start groups, dogs must be kept on a lead, bring your own cup.

name: Napoleon-Mijlenloop
price_range: gratis voor kinderen tot 12 jaar en framerunners, anders niet vermeld
description: The Napoleon Miles Run takes place on October 11 in Den Helder and offers a unique running experience through a historic area with forts and defensive works from the time of Napoleon. Participants can choose between distances of 5 or 10 miles (8 or 16 km), and there is also a special youth run of 1.3 or 2.6 km. The route follows the Helderse Linie and offers an impressive setting of fortifications, bunkers, and the historic line dike. This run is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners and is known as one of the most enjoyable runs in the Netherlands.
course_highlights: Route along the Helderse Linie, passing old forts and defensive works
Impressive setting of fortifications, bunkers, and the historic line dike
Distances from 1.3 km to 16 km, suitable for all levels
additional: Registration is available in advance via inschrijven.nl or on site. The run can be completed recreationally or timed, and is open to everyone from seasoned runners to beginners. Advance registration via inschrijven.nl, course along historic sites, Pasta Party afterwards

name: Spelderholtloop
description: The Spelderholt Run takes place on Sunday, October 11, 2026, at Parc Spelderholt in Beekbergen. This running event is suitable for everyone, young and old, with or without a disability. The start and finish are on the grounds of Parc Spelderholt. The shorter distances (500 meters and 2 kilometers) take place on the grounds, while the longer distances (5 and 10 kilometers) go through the forest. Each distance has its own start time, and participants are advised to arrive at least half an hour before the start to collect their race bib.
course_highlights: 500-meter and 2-kilometer courses on the grounds of Parc Spelderholt
5- and 10-kilometer runs through the forest
Start and finish on the grounds of Parc Spelderholt
additional: Each distance has its own start time. Arrive at least half an hour before the start to collect your race bib. Parking is available at the entrance to the grounds. All ages can participate. Registration is available in advance and on the day; parking at Parc Spelderholt.

name: Vestingloop Edam
location: Vestingwerken Edam, Edam, North Holland, Netherlands
description: The Vestingloop Edam is a traditional running race held along Edam’s old fortifications. Since the first edition in 1954, when the distance was 5 kilometres, the route has remained a fixed feature despite changes to the distances. The race offers several distances, including children’s races, a 3-mile fun run and a 10 km race. The finish is on Baandervesting near the chain bridge, while the longer distances start on Noordervesting. The Vestingloop is known for its changeable weather and friendly atmosphere for both recreational and competitive runners.
course_highlights: Route along Edam’s old fortifications
Finish on Baandervesting, near the chain bridge
The 10 km and 3-mile races start on Noordervesting
additional: For the 10 km and 3-mile races, times are recorded using a chip attached to the race number. Children’s races use shoe chips. OJC participants can take part for free, but must report to registration to collect a shoe chip. Free parking is available, and showers are available in the changing rooms. Medals are awarded to the first three boys and girls in the children’s races. Cash prizes can be won in various age categories in the 10 km. Course along the old fortifications, registration via an online platform, free parking and showers available.

name: Culture Run Woerden
description: The Culture Run Woerden celebrates its fifth anniversary and is a unique fun run bringing together sport, culture and Woerden’s rich history. During this enjoyable run, you’ll discover the city centre in a surprising way, not only passing well-known places but also going right through iconic and cultural buildings. The combination of exercise, culture and Woerden’s characteristic sociable atmosphere makes this event popular with both residents and visitors. With two distances of 5 and 10 kilometres, suitable for walking or running, it’s accessible to all ages. The start and finish are at Technohub Woerden, and the course is made extra festive with acts and entertainment.
course_highlights: Course through Woerden city centre
Right through iconic and cultural buildings
Surprising acts and entertainment along the route
additional: The Culture Run is a fun run where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km, walking or running. The event is suitable for all ages, families and groups of friends. The number of race entries is limited due to capacity constraints at various locations along the route. The start and finish are at Technohub Woerden. The event is made extra festive with surprising acts and entertainment along and on the route. Course through the city centre and cultural buildings, entertainment along the route, two distances (5 and 10 km), walking or running.

description: De 15 van Wassenaar is an atmospheric running event taking place on Sunday, 11 October 2026. Participants can choose between a distance of 15 kilometres or 7.5 kilometres, both of which run through Wassenaar’s village centre, estates and villa neighbourhoods. The event combines a sporting challenge with a festive atmosphere, including refreshments along the way, a medal and an after-party to celebrate the achievement. The race is organised with a focus on charitable causes and an engaged crowd along the scenic course.
course_highlights: Route through the village centre, estates and villa neighbourhoods
Refreshments along the way, with 2 drink stations and a fruit point
Enthusiastic crowd along the scenic course
additional: All participants receive refreshments along the way, a race bib, a medal, fruit and their first drink at the finish. There is a staffed cloakroom and an after-party. The minimum age is 16 for the 7.5 km and 18 for the 15 km. There are 2 drink stations and a fruit point along the way. The route will be closed to traffic, with traffic marshals and temporary closures. Registration via the website; donations to charitable causes are possible. Start time is 14:30. Minimum age is 16 or 18. A medal and after-party are included.

name: Rondje Bussloo
description: Rondje Bussloo is a welcoming running event around the Bussloo recreation area, organised by the team behind Rondje Oeken. The courses for both distances follow paved paths through varied scenery of water, woodland and open fields, and are suitable for both recreational and experienced runners. The start and finish are at Strandhuys De Enk in Wilp, which also has a welcoming hospitality venue. The event is known for its sporty, friendly atmosphere and takes place on Sunday 11 October 2026 at 10:30.
course_highlights: Course on paved paths through varied scenery of water, woodland and open fields
Start and finish at Strandhuys De Enk, with a beautiful view over the water
Suitable for recreational and experienced runners
additional: Race numbers will be available at the race office on the day and will not be sent out in advance. Parking at Bussloo costs €3.50 and must be paid digitally when driving out through the barrier. Toilets are available at Strandhuys De Enk. There is a welcoming hospitality venue at the start and finish where supporters can cheer on runners. Fun for all ages, a route with different starting points, route markers, and use of the Strava app for route tracking.
